functions.not_measured: A POST carrying a real tenant_id was deliberately NOT sent. It would insert a pending row into the live nedarim_transactions table and, worse, rewrite payment_meta on whatever donation_id/order_id the body named. The finding is established from the deployed bundle plus the four probes above.
functions.finding: Two things follow from the missing gate. (a) Any anonymous caller can name any donation_id or order_id in the body; the function updates that row's payment_method/payment_meta with service_role and never checks who owns it. (b) The row it writes to nedarim_transactions binds a fresh our_payment_id to that same donation_id/order_id. nedarim-webhook then matches an incoming IPN on our_payment_id (Param2) and sets payment_status='captured' / status='paid' on the bound row. So a stranger can bind a ₪1 payment of their own to somebody else's real order and have the legitimate Nedarim callback mark that order paid.

functions.verdict: by design open, but it is the second half of #196
functions.gate: IP allowlist against Nedarim Plus's callers; a non-Nedarim IP is rejected — and the rejection itself writes a rejected_ip row, which is why no sweep has ever POSTed to it.
functions.note: Not the hole. It is the mechanism that turns the create-payment hole into a paid order: it trusts the our_payment_id -> donation_id/order_id binding that create-payment wrote without authentication.
